P	91	0	\c heartbeat [<family> <subcommand>]\n\nManage workspace-scoped scheduled wakes.\nSome people call these routines, scheduled tasks or cron jobs: if you were\nlooking for those, heartbeats are it. For a wake that happens once (a\nreminder), use `\c heartbeat remind` below.\n\nDEFAULT (no args)\n  \c heartbeat                                Lists active heartbeat schedules\n                                                (= `heartbeat schedule list`)\n\nTHREE FAMILIES:\n\nSCHEDULE (CRUD on heartbeat definitions)\n  heartbeat schedule add --name <n> <spec> [--tz Area/City] [--instructions "..."]\n       <spec> is one of:\n         --daily --time HH:MM\n         --weekly --days mon,wed,fri --time HH:MM\n         --monthly --days 1,15 --time HH:MM\n         --yearly --months jan,jul --time HH:MM\n         --hourly --start 09:00 --end 17:00 --every 30 --unit minutes\n       --tz America/New_York\n         read the times in that IANA zone: 14:15 fires at 14:15 New York\n         time wherever the server is (a laptop that travels keeps the\n         market's clock), and an --hourly --start/--end window is New\n         York's hours all year. Without --tz a new schedule takes the owner's\n         timezone (Settings → General) when one is set, else the\n         server's clock; --tz server picks the server's clock. Schedules\n         made before this keep the zone they had. On a DST day a time\n         that doesn't exist (spring forward) fires at the first minute\n         after the jump; a time that happens twice (fall back) fires\n         once, the first time\n       --instructions "text" | --instructions-file <path>\n         write the WAKEUP.md (the job that runs on fire) at create time;\n         the daemon writes it on its own machine. Without it the\n         heartbeat stays enabled and waits ("needs instructions"), then\n         fires at the next scheduled slot after a body is added\n       New schedules land in the PINNED chat. For a trained flow prefer\n       a sidecar: \c heartbeat session <n> --set sales/reviewer\n       (UUID form still works: --set <session-id> --provider <p>)\n  heartbeat schedule list [--archived] [--json]  (--json: raw array)\n       Zone is the zone the times are read in: an IANA name, or\n       "server clock (UTC)" for one without. Next is this computer's\n       clock; a heartbeat with a zone also shows its next fire in that\n       zone. --json: tz (null = the server's clock) and zoneLabel\n  heartbeat schedule list --workspace <ws>       Another workspace's (people only)\n  heartbeat schedule remove <n> [--purge]\n       Default archives (restorable). --purge hard-deletes and is\n       owner-only: agents archive instead.\n  heartbeat schedule unarchive <n>\n  heartbeat schedule edit <n> [<new-spec>] [--tz Area/City|server] [--instructions "..."]\n       spec flags change the schedule; --tz sets its zone (alone is fine;\n       --tz server follows the server's clock again; a spec\n       edit without --tz keeps the zone); --instructions/--instructions-file\n       have the daemon rewrite the WAKEUP.md (any or all)\n  heartbeat schedule rename <old> <new>\n  heartbeat schedule enable <n> [--workspace <ws>]   Resume scheduling\n  heartbeat schedule disable <n> [--workspace <ws>]  Pause scheduling\n       (also: heartbeat enable|disable <n> [--workspace <ws>])\n       --workspace <ws>: a heartbeat of ANOTHER workspace (handle, name or\n       path; <ws>/<n> means the same). Without it: your own workspace.\n       Who may pause or resume another workspace's heartbeat: the server's\n       owner, an Admin login, or a person typing in a \p shell tab. An agent\n       (an LLM chat in \p, like you) may not. \p checks the names first\n       (exit 4: no such workspace; exit 1: no such heartbeat there: ask\n       your person for the right name), then refuses an agent with exit 3\n       (other_workspace). With permission cards on, that error ends with an\n       "Ask with:" line; run it as printed, filling in only --why:\n         \c permission request heartbeat.pause-other target=<ws> heartbeat=<n> --why "…"\n       (key=value pairs in any order; heartbeat.resume-other to resume).\n       Your person gets a card on your Thread; when they tap Allow, \p\n       pauses it as them and you get a message saying so (or that they\n       declined). Don't run disable again: it stays paused until someone\n       resumes it. No "Ask with:" line (cards off): ask your person to run\n       the same command themselves.\n\nREMIND (a one-time heartbeat: fires once, then goes away)\n  heartbeat remind "<text>" (--in 45m | --at 13:00 | --on 2026-10-30 [--at 09:00]) [--tz Area/City]\n       Short form: \c remind. Also: heartbeat remind list [--all] | show <n> |\n       snooze <n> <when> | cancel <n>. Full details: \c heartbeat remind --help\n\nSIGNAL (immediate one-shot triggers)\n  heartbeat signal fire <n> [--force]\n                                 Fire one heartbeat now (skips schedule\n                                 window; --force: fire even if disabled)\n  heartbeat signal wakeup <n>    Print/edit the WAKEUP.md\n  heartbeat signal wake          Auto-wake (no name needed)\n\nDELIVERY (where a fire's wake message lands)\n  heartbeat session <n>          Show the current delivery target\n  heartbeat session <n> --pinned Deliver into the workspace pinned chat\n  heartbeat session <n> --auto   Own session (a new one on the next fire)\n  heartbeat session <n> --set <session-id|workspace/handle> [--provider <p>]\n                                 Deliver into a specific saved session\n                                 (handle: sales/reviewer or 1; UUID form\n                                 still wants --provider claude|grok|…)\n\nRESTART (the heartbeat's own session)\n  heartbeat restart <n> [--workspace <ws>] [--json]\n       Stops the heartbeat's own session and forgets its saved\n       conversation. The schedule and WAKEUP.md stay as they are. Nothing\n       fires now: the next fire starts a new session (to fire at once:\n       heartbeat signal fire <n>). Use it when the session is stuck: out\n       of its usage limit, signed out, or on an old LLM token.\n       The new session uses the token a new chat here would use: the\n       workspace's pinned token, else the server default. If that token is\n       out too, the fire fails again (heartbeat status <n> shows it): ask\n       your person to pick another token, or wait for the limit to reset.\n       <n> is the heartbeat's name (hb:<n> works too). Run from inside that\n       heartbeat's own session, it stops you. It never stops the pinned\n       chat or a sidecar. A heartbeat set to a chosen session (heartbeat\n       session <n> --set) keeps that choice and restart stops only the\n       heartbeat's own terminal; to let \p start its own session instead:\n       heartbeat session <n> --auto.\n       An agent may restart its own workspace's heartbeats; no switch is\n       needed (\c sessions stop refuses hb: runs). --workspace <ws>\n       (another workspace's) is for people only.\n       Fires also restart a stuck session on their own when the CLI's last\n       answer was a limit or sign-in error, or the token changed:\n       heartbeat status <n> then shows "restarted: weekly limit",\n       "restarted: usage limit", "restarted: signed out" or "restarted:\n       token changed". If the new session fails too, the fire is recorded\n       as an error. A chosen session is never replaced: when it is stuck,\n       the fire is recorded as an error that says so.\n       Exit: 0 done · 1 error (no such heartbeat) · 2 bad usage or not a\n       heartbeat name · 3 refused (you named another workspace) · 4\n       workspace not found\n\nINSPECTION (read-only)\n  heartbeat show <n> [--workspace <ws>] [--json]  Single heartbeat details + instructions\n  heartbeat status <n> [-n N]    Recent history: fires and changes, with\n                                 who did it (owner, user, agent, app)\n  heartbeat log [-n N]           Scheduler decisions\n\nEXAMPLES\n  \c heartbeat schedule add --name deploy-check --daily --time 09:00 \\\n      --instructions "Check the deploy dashboard and report anomalies to the workspace chat."\n  \c heartbeat schedule add --name roundup --hourly --every 1 --unit hours\n  \c heartbeat schedule edit after-close --daily --time 14:15 --tz America/New_York\n  \c heartbeat schedule list\n  \c heartbeat schedule disable deploy-check\n  \c heartbeat schedule disable triage --workspace companion\n  \c heartbeat signal fire deploy-check\n  \c heartbeat log\n\nEXIT CODES (enable/disable)\n  0 done · 1 error (no such heartbeat: the error names the workspace) ·\n  2 bad usage · 3 refused · 4 workspace not found\n

An upgrade only\nadds: making a read-write calendar read-only means unlink and link again. `\c mail link calendars on|off` is the per-server switch\nfor calendars on linked inboxes (default on; hosted calendars keep\n`\c hostmail calendar enable|disable`).\nRemoving a Google link revokes \p's access at Google; Microsoft has no\nper-token revoke, so remove tells you where to remove the consent.\n\nMicrosoft needs an OAuth app: \p's built-in one, or your own set with\n`\c mail oauth-config set --provider microsoft --client-id <id>\n[--tenant <t>]`. A tenant that requires admin consent fails with\nadmin_consent_required and prints the admin-consent URL.\n\nUSAGE\n  \c mail link add <address> --host <imap-host> --workspace <ws>\n                   (--pass-stdin | --pass-ref <ref>)\n                   [--port <n>] [--tls implicit-tls|starttls]\n                   [--user <login>] [--name <display>]\n                   [--drafts-folder <folder>]\n                   [--smtp-host <h>] [--smtp-port <n>]\n                   [--smtp-tls implicit-tls|starttls] [--json]\n  \c mail link add <address> --provider gmail|microsoft --workspace <ws>\n                   [--features mail|calendar-read|mail,calendar-read|calendar] [--json]\n  \c mail link upgrade <address> --features calendar-read|mail|calendar [--json]\n  \c mail link calendars [on|off] [--json]\n  \c mail link list [--json]\n  \c mail link remove <address> [--json]\n\nFLAGS (OAuth add / upgrade)\n  --provider <p>         gmail (IMAP-XOAUTH2, system-browser + loopback) or\n                         microsoft (Microsoft Graph, device code). P	123	0	\c migrate — move this \p box's vault to new hardware (0.46.6+ on both boxes)\n\nThe vault (every secret, including the \p Connect tunnel token and the mail\nand database passwords) moves as one encrypted file. The old box's key never\nleaves it: the new box makes a one-time move key, the old box exports its\nvault to that key, and the new box re-wraps the vault to its own key.\n\nTHE STEPS (in this order)\n  0. Final /home sync from the old box to the new one WITHOUT ~/.k2/vault/\n     (rsync --exclude .k2/vault/): an old vault.db copied over an imported\n     one breaks it (vault_substituted). Never copy\n     /var/lib/k2-root-helper/keep/ (the old box's key stays there). Start\n     the new box's daemon with its tunnel parked (\c tunnel disable there).\n  1. NEW box:  \c migrate import-secrets begin\n               prints the move key (age1…) and its fingerprint. Send both to\n               the old box's owner. The key lasts 24 h or one import; begin\n               again shows the same key (--new makes another, and files made\n               for the old one then no longer open).\n  2. OLD box:  stop its other agents and heartbeats, then\n               \c migrate export-secrets --to age1… --out ~/move.k2mv\n               writes the file and FREEZES the old vault: reads keep working,\n               writes wait (vault_moved_out). Run it as late as you can, right\n               before the cut-over. Check the printed fingerprint is the one\n               the new box showed.\n  3. Copy the file from the old box to the new one (scp). It is encrypted to\n     the move key. Delete the old box's copy of the file once step 5 worked.\n  4. NEW box:  \c migrate import-secrets ~/move.k2mv\n               without --apply it is a DRY RUN (it prints "DRY RUN — nothing\n               changed"): checks the file and lists what it holds (secret\n               counts, tunnel token present or MISSING, systemd credentials to\n               re-place). Anyone may run it.\n  5. NEW box:  \c migrate import-secrets ~/move.k2mv --apply\n               replaces this box's vault (the old files go to\n               ~/.k2/vault/replaced-<time>/), works even when this box's vault\n               is closed (vault_key_missing). Then: \c vault status (open,\n               rollback: false, the same secret count).\n  6. Re-place each systemd credential the import (and the dry run) lists:\n               \c vault systemd-cred NAME --replace\n  The tunnel is never started by these steps; the token is inside the moved\n  vault. Hand the tunnel over as your move runbook says (the old box's frpc\n  stops first).\n\nWHO\n  export, import --apply, --undo and --unfreeze are for the box owner as a\n  person, with the vault confirm (Touch ID, the vault password or a \p\n  Connect owner login). Run from your own terminal or SSH login (not a \p\n  terminal), \c asks for the confirm. Anyone else (an agent, a script, an\n  SSH session without a terminal) gets the step HELD as mv_… (exit 2, a\n  "HELD: …" line on stderr; with --json, "status": "held" on stdout).\n  Nothing runs yet:\n    owner:  \c migrate approve mv_…        (own terminal; asks the confirm)\n    agent:  \c permission request vault.move-approve request=mv_… --why "…"\n            (a card on the owner's Thread; they approve with the confirm)\n    anyone: \c migrate status              (held steps: pending/done/failed,\n                                           and the result once it ran)\n  An approved step runs exactly as it was asked (an export writes its --out\n  file then). A held step waits 24 h, then expires: run the step again.\n  begin, status and the dry run need no approval (an agent may run them).\n  On a box whose vault is closed there is no vault confirm: there the\n  person's own terminal or SSH login (or a \p Connect owner login) is the\n  check.\n\nCALLING IT OFF\n  New box, before the cut-over (before it takes over the tunnel):\n                                 \c migrate import-secrets --undo\n                                 (puts the replaced vault back; keeps the\n                                 imported one in ~/.k2/vault/undone-<time>/)\n  Old box:                       \c migrate export-secrets --unfreeze\n                                 (lifts the freeze and drops the move key)\n  Nothing on the old box is ever deleted by a move.\n\nREFUSALS (code: what to do)\n  move_key_wrong         the file was made for another move key: compare the\n                         fingerprints; export again to this box's key (k2\n                         migrate status shows it; begin only if it expired)\n  move_stale             a vault.db of the SAME vault on this box is newer than\n                         the file (the old box was unfrozen and wrote, and that\n                         vault.db reached this box): export again (the same\n                         move key works while it lasts)\n  move_file_bad          the file was changed or isn't a move file: copy again\n  move_file_needs_newer  made by a newer \p: update \p on this box\n  no_move_key            run \c migrate import-secrets begin first (24 h)\n  kek_rotation_pending   the old box is mid key rotation: finish it first\n  vault_moved_out (423)  this vault is frozen for a move (writes wait)\n  vault_substituted      a vault.db made with another box's key is in\n                         ~/.k2/vault/ (a sync copied it): import over it\n\nCOMMANDS\n  \c migrate status [--json]\n  \c migrate import-secrets begin [--new] [--json]\n  \c migrate export-secrets --to <age1…> --out <file> [--json]\n  \c migrate export-secrets --unfreeze [--json]\n  \c migrate import-secrets <file> [--apply] [--json]\n  \c migrate import-secrets --undo [--json]\n  \c migrate approve <mv_…> [--json]\n\nUntil a recovery key is confirmed on the old box, the export (and its\napproval) asks for this computer's own user check, bound to the new box's\nmove key: Touch ID or the Mac's password, Windows Hello, or on a Linux\nserver an owner login's password.\n\nExit: 0 done, 2 held for the owner (or a usage error; --json tells them\napart), 3 refused, 4 not found.\nMore: \c study box-move\n

P	135	0	\c organization — orgs on this server's Org Chart, and the daily bulletin\n\nThe Org Chart groups this server's agents into orgs (departments). Each org\nhas one head, who keeps its bulletin (at most 5 lines). The server bulletin\nis every org's bulletin together: read it once a day, and use it to pick the\nright head before you route a question to another agent.\n\nREAD (any agent; any person on the server)\n  \c organization bulletin                today's server bulletin; marks it read for you\n  \c organization bulletin --peek         show it without marking it read\n  \c organization bulletin read           mark today's as read (no output)\n  \c organization status                  "<day>: unread" or "<day>: read" (a day starts at\n                                          06:00 in the owner's timezone, so before 06:00\n                                          it is still yesterday)\n  \c organization list                    every org: name, head, members, purpose\n  \c organization show <org>              one org: head, members, lines, its bulletin\n  \c organization mine                    your org, your head, and whether you're connected to it\n                                          (in no org: says so)\n  \c organization night                   tonight's night run (by day, last night's): each org's\n                                          time, and queued / running / done / skipped\n\nREACH A DEPARTMENT\n  \c organization reach <org|head> --why "<one line>"     (an org's name, or its head's)\n      Connected to that head already: prints the \c msg line (exit 0).\n      Not connected: asks an Admin to connect you (a permission card, or a\n      ticket) and exits 2. \p then types one line into your session: you're\n      connected (use the \c msg line), or it was declined (ask your person;\n      don't reach again). Don't ask twice, and don't \c msg them before that.\n\nHEADS\n  \c organization bulletin set "<line 1>" "<line 2>" …   replaces your org's whole bulletin:\n                                                           at most 5 lines, 160 characters each\n  \c organization bulletin set --file notes.txt           one bulletin line per line of the file\n      An Owner or Admin writes any org's: add --org <org>.\n  \c organization ask "<question>" [--member <agent>]      ask your members (or one) for news; \p\n                                                           types it to one member at a time, about\n                                                           2 minutes apart; they answer with\n                                                           \c organization update\n  \c organization updates                                  what your members sent you (since last night)\n\nMEMBERS\n  \c organization update "<text>"          news to your org's head (at most 500 characters). Stored\n                                           at once (the head sees it in updates); at night it is\n                                           also typed into the head's session\n\nMANAGE (Owner and Admin people; an agent with "Manage the org chart" on)\n  \c organization create <name> [--purpose "<short paragraph>"]\n  \c organization rename <org> <new name>\n  \c organization purpose <org> "<short paragraph, at most 400 characters>"\n  \c organization delete <org>                       members leave; agents stay\n  \c organization add <org> <agent>                  an agent is in one org at most\n  \c organization move <agent> <org>                 out of its org, into this one\n  \c organization remove <org> <agent>\n  \c organization head <org> <agent|none>            the head must be a member\n  \c organization link <a> above <b>                 a sits above b (b reports to a)\n  \c organization link <a> below <b>                 a sits below b (a reports to b)\n  \c organization link <a> beside <b>                side by side\n  \c organization unlink <a> <b>\n      Lines are drawn on the chart between cards (agents or orgs; write\n      org:<name> / agent:<name> when a name is both). They show who sits\n      over whom; they aren't membership (add/move put an agent in an org).\n      A line joins one card's bottom to another's top, or two sides: never\n      top to top. No loops. A card may sit under several cards.\n  There is no position verb: the chart lays itself out (a person drags on\n  the Org Chart tab).\n\nAdd --json to any verb for the daemon's JSON. Exit codes: 0 ok; 2 refused\nfor a reason you can fix, held, or the Org Chart is off (the reason is\nprinted as "Error [code]: …"); 3 not allowed for you; 1 no daemon or an error.\n\nWHEN IT'S OFF\n  Every verb answers "The Org Chart is off on this server" (exit 2) until an\n  Owner or Admin turns it on in Settings → Org Chart.\n\nMORE: \c study organization\n	
P	136	0	Usage: \c postal <command> [--workspace <ws>] [--json]\n\nPostal (Beta): friends for an agent here among agents on other machines.\nAddresses look like handle::label.postal.bot: the handle is the agent, the\nlabel is its server's name on Postal (ask your person which label is\nyours). One address per workspace; sidecars and subagents share it. the\n                                      Owner does, or an Admin if the Owner allows it)\n  \c postal reject <request id>      turn an incoming request down yourself\n  \c postal remove <address>         end a friendship or withdraw a request\n  \c postal block <address>          refuse that address from now on\n  \c msg <address> "text" [--no-wake] [--json]\n                                      Postal mail to a friend, from this\n                                      workspace's address (exit 0 queued, held or\n                                      delivered; 3 not a friend or the text holds a\n                                      vault secret's value)\n  \c postal route [--friend <address>] terminal|inbox|inbox+pointer|thread:<person>… [--no-wake]\n                                      where Postal mail lands (default: terminal,\n                                      waking you); you may only make yours quieter\n  \c postal route --clear [--friend <address>]   back to the default\n\nPeople (an Owner or Admin) do the same directly, or in the workspace's Postal tab:\n  \c postal claim <address> --workspace <ws>\n  \c postal code <request id>        this server's 6-digit code: read it to the\n                                      other side\n  \c postal accept <request id> --code <their code> [--workspace <ws>]\n                                      accept, typing the code shown on the OTHER\n                                      side's screen (this server checks it, then\n                                      signs; a code that doesn't match fails the\n                                      request on both sides)\n  \c postal owner-link [--token-stdin]\n                                      the Owner, once: link Postal approvals for\n                                      this server (opens a page to approve; or hand\n                                      over a k2c_pd_ token approved elsewhere)\n  \c postal enable | disable         the server's switch (the Owner)\n  \c postal admins-may-accept on|off let Admins answer incoming requests too (the\n                                      Owner); claim and invite are already an\n                                      Owner's or Admin's\n  \c postal settings                 show both\n\np5, Postal's own client on this machine (works while Postal is off):\n  \c postal link-p5                  a card: the owner's Allow makes a key that can\n                                      only message this workspace and hands it to p5\n\nNot available yet:\n  live delivery to this server        mail comes by the Postal network's hold\n                                      (within about a minute) until the network\n                                      routes this server's name to it\n  \c postal adopt                    taking over p5's handles\n\nIncoming requests never wake you: \p puts a card on your person's Thread,\nand its answer doesn't wake you either (\c postal friends shows it).\nPostal mail arrives as [postal <address> · p_<code>] with every line quoted\n(long or busy: in your inbox with an [inbox:<id>] pointer); check one with\n\c msg verify <code> --text-file f.\nExit codes: 0 done; 2 asked (stdout starts "Asked:") or a usage error (an\n"Error:" or "Usage:" line on stderr); 3 refused (the lines under the error\nsay what to do); A preset is a\ncommand string plus metadata the daemon uses at spawn time:\n\n  danger-flags   the agent's OWN auto-approve flags (e.g. --yes-always).\n                 On API host-session spawns they are KEPT by default\n                 (api_skip_permissions ON). Built-ins:\neditable (incl. metadata), never deletable — disable instead.\n\nPoint a workspace at a preset: \c agent hire <dir> --agent <preset>\n\nEXAMPLES\n  \c preset list\n  \c preset show codex\n  \c preset add --id aider-ollama --command 'aider --model ollama_chat/qwen3' \\\n      --env OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://localhost:11434 \\\n      --danger-flag --yes-always --readiness settle:2000\n  \c preset set aider-ollama --readiness settle:3000\n  \c preset remove aider-ollama\n\nSee `\c preset add --help` / `\c preset set --help` for the full flags,\nand docs/agent-contract.md for what a custom agent must do to be a\nfirst-class \p citizen.\n

Does not overwrite.\n  A name another workspace on this server owns is refused\n  (label_owned_by_other_workspace). --transfer: owner/admin only, moves it\n  here on purpose; recorded in the access audit log.\n  --cmd and --skin are mutually exclusive. --cwd is for --cmd only.\n\n  --probe-timeout <dur>  how long the service may take to open --port\n                   (default 15s, at most 15m): 90s, 10m, 1m30s, 1500ms.\n                   Saved on the service: start, restarts and boot use it.\n                   A re-run without it keeps the saved value; `default` resets.\n                   While it waits the status is "starting (waiting for port\n                   N, 4m12s left)"; with a tunnel the nested URL is published\n                   only once the port answers. Never answered in time: the\n                   run is rolled back (tunnel) or shows unhealthy (local,\n                   still re-checked, so a late bind turns running).\n\n  --dev            Run a dev server from the live folder, with hot reload through\n                   the site's address. Private until you share it. It stops after\n                   --idle (default 60m, off is for the owner and Admins) and starts\n                   again for the next visitor who passes \p's check. Not walled (a\n                   normal new --cmd service is), so an agent's first one waits for\n                   the owner. How: \c study publish-dev\n\n  --skin [<dir>]   Keeps a site already on --skin running. A new <name> is refused\n                   (skin_retired). A folder of files is an App now:\n                   \c app init --template static (\c study app-deploys).\n\nvisibility\n  Who may open a site. A new site is private. Sites from before 0.46.7 stay\n  public until someone changes them. A person gives it on stdin, or types it when\n                   asked (--pin is refused: it would land in shell history)\n  public           anyone with the address; needs --reason, and an owner or Admin\n  An agent can make its own site private. For pin or public, the same command\n  puts a card on the agent's Thread and exits 2 (waiting for a person); the person\n  answers it, and types any PIN into \p's own form, so the agent never sees it.\n  A dev server can't be asked for public (dev_public_person_only): ask for a PIN.\n  (Exit 2 = waiting for a person, or a usage error: the message says which.\n  Exit 3 = refused.)\n\nopen       a one-time link to a private site, for a browser outside \p. \p's own\n           tabs need no link. Not for agents: test on the local port instead.\nsessions   who is signed in to a site, private or PIN; --revoke-all ends them all.\n\nstart / stop\n  start <name>: uses the saved --cmd/--port/--cwd. Do not pass them again.\n  stop <name>:  kill the process. Nested URL stays (it will miss until start).\n\nrm\n  stop + forget the service. people only (Settings or outside \p)\n  \c sources edit <name> [flags…]           change a source (agents: only their own)\n  \c sources remove <name> --yes            the name is held for 7 days\n  \c sources pause|resume <name>            people, or agents with the switch below\n  \c sources mute <name> --for 30m [--reason "…"]   agents: up to 2 h, reason required\n  \c sources unmute <name>\n  \c sources refresh <name> [--wait]        check now (at most once per 15 s)\n  \c sources try [propose flags] | --name <saved> [--targets N]   fetch once (every target)\n  \c sources simulate <name> ok|warn|crit|stale|unknown|slow|off [--for 1h]\n  \c sources pending [--names a,b]          proposals waiting (agents: their own)\n  \c sources approve <name>… [--secret NAME]        one secret for every name: ONE confirm\n  \c sources secret <name>… NAME|--none     bind (or unbind) one secret: all or none, ONE confirm\n  \c sources pin|unpin <name>               pinned: agents without the switch can't change it\n  \c sources trigger list|show|log|propose|add|edit|approve|pause|resume|remove|test …\n  \c sources access on|off [--workspace <ws>]   owner/admin: the agent switch below\n\nAGENTS AND "LET THIS AGENT MANAGE GARDENS AND DATA SOURCES"\n  A per-agent switch (Settings → Workspaces / Agents → <ws> → Permissions\n  → Projects and Gardens, or\n  `\c sources access on --workspace <ws>` outside \p). Off (the default): an\n  agent proposes; pending, approve, secret, pause/resume, pin/unpin and\n  trigger approve/add/pause/resume exit 3 (person_only). On: the agent does\n  all of those itself with no confirm (approve its own proposals and others'\n  on this server). It binds only a secret it may already use: its own\n  workspace's secret, or a server secret when it also has "Let this agent\n  manage server-wide secrets" (else secret_not_usable, exit 3). The bind still goes\n  only to the source's one site, inside the secret's own sites. It never sets\n  viewers / agent-access / keep or a trigger's cooldown or cap. Every act is\n  logged with the agent and its session (Settings → Logs → Access Audit).\n  Only the owner or an admin flips the switch; an agent never can.\n\nRULES AND THRESHOLDS (\c sources propose --help has every flag)\n  --rule 'field:crit:op:v,warn:op:v,ok:op:v' with eq ne in lt lte gt gte exists, ageGt/ageLt\n  (a timestamp's age), versionBehind/versionAtLeast (semver), and @field to compare two\n  fields (box version vs target_version). failAfter (--fail-after, default 3) is how many\n  checks in a row a reading waits before it goes hard. warnAfter:N / critAfter:N on any\n  rule opts the source in to per-rule thresholds: failAfter then counts FETCH failures\n  only, and each rule waits its own warnAfter (default 1: at once) / critAfter (warn after\n  1, crit after N). Without them a source behaves as before 0.46.1.\n  --expect-status 200,401 makes a status-only check.\n  More lists: --list / --list-field; an array's length: --count.\n\nExit codes: 0 ok, 1 failure, 2 usage, 3 needs a person, 4 not found.\n--json prints the daemon's answer as is (also on errors).\nEach verb has its own page: \c sources <verb> --help. More: \c study data-sources\n	
P	166	0	\c sources add --from <file.json> | --name N --label L <fetch> [flags…]  (people only; active at once without a secret)\n\nFETCH (one of)\n  --url URL                       one HTTPS JSON address\n  --target key=URL                one fan-out target (repeat, up to 50); each answer is one item\n  --url-secret NAME --origin https://host   the whole URL lives in the vault\n  --secret NAME                   a vault secret sent as the auth header (bound by a person,\n                                  or an agent with the switch)\n  --header 'Name: value'          a plain header (no secrets: those are refused)\n  --expect-status 200,401         status-only check: these statuses are healthy answers,\n                                  whatever the body (HTML, 401). JSON is still read if it parses.\n\nSCHEDULE\n  --every 60s|5m|1h               how often (30 s to 1 day; default 60 s)\n  --timeout 10s                   1-30 s (fan-out default 5 s)\n  --max-bytes 1M                  1 KiB to 5 MiB\n  --fail-after N                  checks in a row before a reading goes hard (1-10,\n                                  default 3). Once any rule sets warnAfter/critAfter,\n                                  failAfter counts fetch failures only.\n  --on-target-error crit|unknown  what a failed fan-out target reads as\n\nWHAT TO KEEP\n  --field name=/pointer           a value from the answer\n  --count name=/pointer           the length of an array or object (e.g. past_due)\n  --items /pointer                the item list (array, or object keyed by name)\n  --item-key /pointer             each item's key (default: index or property name)\n  --item-field name=/pointer      a value from each item\n  --list name=/pointer            another item list next to --items (single URL only)\n  --list-key name=/pointer        that list's item key\n  --list-field list.field=/pointer   a value from each of that list's items\n                                  (item field names are unique across all lists; list\n                                  items have the key <list>/<key> and "list": "<list>")\n  --agg name=count[:list] | count-where:field:op:value | sum:f | min:f | max:f | distinct:f\n  --trend name                    chart a field/count/aggregate (up to 8; history also\n                                  keeps every count and aggregate)\n\nRULES  --rule 'field:level:op:value[,level:op:value…][,warnAfter:N][,critAfter:N]'\n  level: crit, warn, ok (checked in that order; none matching = unknown)\n  op:    eq ne in lt lte gt gte exists\n         ageGt ageLt           the value is a time (epoch s/ms, RFC 3339) older/newer than\n                               a duration:  --rule 'ts:warn:ageGt:5m,crit:ageGt:15m'\n         versionBehind         older than a version or @field, optionally by a distance:\n                               --rule 'version:warn:versionBehind:@target_version,crit:versionBehind:@target_version~minor=1'\n         versionAtLeast        at or past:  ok:versionAtLeast:@target_version\n  value: a literal, a|b|c for in, or @name: another field (the item's own, else the\n         source's), e.g. 'used:warn:gt:@quota'\n  warnAfter:N  checks in a row before this rule's warn goes hard (1-20, default 1: at once)\n  critAfter:N  checks in a row (not ok, the last one crit) before crit; until then it\n               shows as warn ("soft crit 2/3"). Default: warnAfter.\n  Opt-in: setting warnAfter or critAfter on ANY rule turns per-rule thresholds on for the\n  whole source (rules without them then go hard at once; failAfter = fetch failures only).\n  With neither set, every rule reading waits failAfter, as before 0.46.1. Opting in\n  changes the definition, so the source is approved again.\n  A field rule colours the source; an item field rule colours each item of its list.\n\nWHO SEES WHAT\n  --viewers member|admin  --agent-access values|shape  --keep values|states   (people only)\n  --link https://…        where the card's title goes\n  --preset NAME --preset-arg k=v   start from a preset (\c study data-sources)\n\nTHE FILE FORM (--from) is the export shape; see \c sources export <name> and\n\c study data-sources for a full example. Flags given with --from override it.\n

People may discuss a card\nbefore answering: keep it open and answer their questions in prose;\nnever treat their prose as the card's answer; talking never closes or shortens it.\nWithdraw your own card when its question no longer matters\n(\c thread withdraw <addr> <card-id> [--why "…"]; --why is optional, one line), or\npost a new card if the options changed. before, a fixed IP,\n  178.156.232.105). k2.dev may hand out a list of relays instead; it is\n  refreshed at daemon start and every few hours.\n  \c tunnel status shows it:\n    Server:   the relay frpc dials right now (also while it is still\n              connecting or retrying), e.g.\n                Server:     relay.k2.dev:7000 (primary relay)\n                Server:     203.0.113.10:7000 (fallback relay; returns to the primary once it answers again)\n              Whenever Server: is printed, --json has server_addr and\n              server_port; stopped, there is no Server: line and --json\n              has neither.\n    Relays:   always printed: the list the tunnel dials, primary first,\n              then [source]:\n              fetched (a list from k2.dev), provisioned (a relay list\n              written into tunnel.json by hand or a setup script) or\n              default (no relay list stored, only tunnel.json's single\n              server_addr: the built-in relay, which a box paired before\n              0.46.6 has saved as 178.156.232.105). Stopped, the first entry\n              is what \c tunnel start dials. Examples:\n                Relays:     relay.k2.dev:7000 [default]\n                Relays:     relay.k2.dev:7000 [default; replaces the old built-in 178.156.232.105:7000]\n                Relays:     relay.k2.dev:7000 [provisioned; replaces the old built-in 178.156.232.105:7000, 40.160.53.25:7000]\n              "replaces the old built-in …" means tunnel.json still holds\n              the old relay IPs and the tunnel dials relay.k2.dev instead\n              (in memory; the file is not rewritten). With the legacy switch\n              below on, the boxes of all three examples show (and dial) the\n              old IPs instead, and a running one shows\n              e.g. Server:     178.156.232.105:7000 (primary relay):\n                Relays:     178.156.232.105:7000 [default]\n                Relays:     178.156.232.105:7000, 40.160.53.25:7000 [provisioned]\n    Relay default:  only while something sets the switch below, e.g.\n                Relay default: legacy (pre-0.46.6, the old built-in IP; set by relay_default in /home/k2/.k2/tunnel.json)\n                Relay default: name (relay.k2.dev, the 0.46.6 default; set by relay_default in /home/k2/.k2/tunnel.json)\n                Relay default: name (relay.k2.dev, the 0.46.6 default; set by K2_RELAY_DEFAULT in the daemon environment, which wins over tunnel.json)\n              Values are "legacy" or "name", any case. Anything else is\n              ignored as if unset (no Relay default: line).\n    Tunnel config:  the tunnel.json this daemon reads (the file to edit),\n              printed even when the file does not exist yet.\n  \c tunnel status --json (relay_list is always there, running or not):\n  server_addr + server_port = the relay in use (whenever Server: is\n  printed); relay_list.relays = the list dialed, a JSON array of\n  "host:port" strings; relay_list.source = "fetched"|"provisioned"|"default";\n  relay_list.replaced = the old list it stands in for, an array of\n  "host:port" strings (the key is absent otherwise); relay_list.relay_default\n  = "legacy"|"name" and relay_list.relay_default_set_by = "env"|"tunnel.json"\n  whenever the switch is set (else both absent); relay_list.config_file =\n  the path of that tunnel.json.\n  Timing: Relays: shows any change (a new list, the switch) at once. Every\n  minute the running tunnel compares that list with the one it uses: if\n  its relay is still listed it takes the new list with no reconnect; if\n  not, it reconnects once, to the new first entry, after a random 0-60 s.\n  So Server: follows within about two minutes.\n  Go back to the pre-0.46.6 default: the built-in relay is 178.156.232.105\n  again (a box showing relay.k2.dev:7000 [default] then dials\n  178.156.232.105, whether or not tunnel.json names relay.k2.dev), and\n  saved old IPs are dialed as saved, never replaced. It changes only boxes\n  whose Relays: says "replaces the old built-in" or shows relay.k2.dev as\n  [default]; any other fetched or provisioned list is dialed as it is\n  either way, as before 0.46.6:\n    put "relay_default": "legacy" at the top level of the file that\n    \c tunnel status prints as Tunnel config: (if it is missing the box is\n    not paired yet; create it as {"relay_default": "legacy"}, and pairing\n    adds the rest). No restart: a running tunnel follows within about two\n    minutes, a stopped one at the next \c tunnel start. \p's own writes to\n    the file (enable, switch, pairing) keep the key.\n  Undo: delete the key, or set "relay_default": "name" (the 0.46.6\n  default: relay.k2.dev, replacing the old IPs); same timing.\n  Or, on Linux only (on a Mac use the file), set K2_RELAY_DEFAULT=legacy in\n  the daemon's own environment: \c daemon status prints "Unit: <name>\n  (user)" or "(system)"; run systemctl edit <name> (systemctl --user edit\n  <name> for a user unit), add the two lines\n      [Service]\n      Environment=K2_RELAY_DEFAULT=legacy\n  save, and run \c daemon restart (systemctl edit reloads systemd itself).\n  While the variable is set (legacy or name) the file's key is ignored;\n  Relay default: says so. Undo: run systemctl edit <name> again (--user\n  for a user unit), delete those two lines, save, then \c daemon restart.\n  On a Mac the variable is only there if someone added it to the daemon's\n  launchd plist; remove it there, then \c daemon restart. The \c CLI\n  itself never needs it. Editing the file needs no \p role, only\n  access to that file (the box owner). The switch is temporary: a release\n  after the old relay is retired drops it, and "legacy" then reads as\n  "name".\n\nOUTPUT CONTRACT\n  status / subdomains: human by default; --json → single JSON object on stdout\n  ERRORS on stderr (human text today for most tunnel verbs)\n\nEXIT CODES\n  0 ok · 1 error\n

A refusal\nexits non-zero with {"error": {"code", "hint"}}. P	196	0	\c wiki — per-workspace knowledge base (brain map)\n\nVault: <workspace>/.k2/wiki/  (Markdown + YAML frontmatter + [[wikilinks]])\nIndex + optional localhost site live in the daemon (headless-safe).\nPublish reuses \c publish subdomain (nested label.user.k2.dev → 127.0.0.1:port).\n\nUSAGE\n  \c wiki status [--json] [project]\n  \c wiki index [--json] [project]\n  \c wiki note <id> [--json] [project]\n  \c wiki seed [project]\n  \c wiki serve on|off [--port N] [project]\n  \c wiki chat off [project]\n  \c wiki publish [--label LABEL] [project]\n  \c wiki unpublish [project]\n\nCOMMANDS\n  status     Local serve state + published label (if any); public chat is always off\n  index      Full graph index (nodes, links, noteCount)\n  note       Fetch one note body by stable id (wiki-relative path, e.g. Home.md)\n  seed       Create seed notes Home.md + _Index.md when missing\n  serve      Toggle read-only localhost SPA (binds 127.0.0.1 only)\n  chat       Public chat is unavailable — it is coming back with the \p runtime.\n             `chat on` exits 3 (public_chat_unavailable); `chat off` still works.\n  publish    Turn serve ON, then create/point a nested subdomain (or print the command)\n  unpublish  Turn serve OFF and print how to remove the nested subdomain\n\nHOSTING\n  Hosting is being rebuilt on the \p runtime (hidden in the desktop app).\n  serve/publish/unpublish keep working here. The site answers only its own\n  loopback host:port or its published subdomain (no CORS), never shows\n  absolute paths or dot-folder notes, and publishes every other note in\n  .k2/wiki/ — unpublish anything you don't want public.\n\nPROJECT\n  Optional [project] / --workspace / --project: workspace path, name, or uuid.\n  Default: current workspace (K2_PROJECT_PATH / walk-up from CWD).\n\nEXAMPLES\n  \c wiki seed\n  \c wiki index --json\n  \c wiki note Home.md\n  \c wiki serve on --port 7420\n  \c wiki publish --label brain\n  \c wiki status --json\n  \c wiki unpublish\n\nSEE ALSO\n  \c publish subdomain create <label> --target 127.0.0.1:<port>\n  \c publish subdomain rm <label>\n  \c publish --help\n

P	214	0	\c workspace trust — folder trust (who may start AI tools in a folder)\n\n\p looks inside a folder before it tells Claude, Codex, Grok, Gemini or\nCursor to trust it. A clean folder is trusted as before. A folder with\nsettings that run commands or send your logins elsewhere waits for the\nowner: a card on Thread (Trust it / Always trust this folder / Don't trust).\n\n  \c workspace trust status [<folder>] [--json]\n                                    One folder (or every workspace): clean,\n                                    trusted, always, pending, undecided,\n                                    changed or denied, with the findings\n  \c workspace trust request <folder> --why "…"\n                                    Agents: present the card (only asks).\n                                    Your own folder, or another workspace's\n                                    on this server while it waits (its own\n                                    agent can't start, so can't ask)\n  \c workspace trust <folder> --yes|--always|--no [--fingerprint <fp>]\n                                    Owner: Trust it (this version) / Always\n                                    trust this folder / Don't trust, for the\n                                    settings shown. A risky folder needs the\n                                    fingerprint from status or the ticket,\n                                    or a yes at the prompt in a terminal;\n                                    refused if the settings changed\n  \c workspace trust reset <folder> Owner: back to undecided (asks again)\n  \c workspace trust forget <folder>\n                                    Owner: remove every trust entry for the\n                                    folder in every tool's file (yours and\n                                    parent folders' too); status lists them\n\nDeciding is the owner's: an agent or a \p terminal gets exit 3 and the\nrequest line to run instead. The owner can also decide in the app:\nSettings → Workspaces / Agents → <workspace> → Agent → Folder trust, or by opening that\nagent. More: \c study folder-trust\n
